environment.description: Same Ktor microservice deployed in namespace 'services' on EKS 1.28. A Cilium-based NetworkPolicy with L3/L4 egress rules is applied at the namespace level. The policy spec uses a combination of CiliumNetworkPolicy CRDs with entity-based selectors: egress is allowed only to pods matching label 'mesh-participant=true' on ports 8080/8443, and to kube-dns (UDP/53). The policy does NOT explicitly mention 169.254.169.254 in a deny rule — instead, it uses a default-deny posture where the allowlist implicitly excludes link-local addresses because the toEndpoints selector cannot match the metadata service (it's not a pod endpoint). The Cilium agent runs in strict mode with policy enforcement set to 'always' and BPF-level datapath. Additionally, the EKS nodes have a secondary iptables chain (inserted by a DaemonSet running kube2iam) that drops packets from pod CIDR to 169.254.169.254 unless the pod annotation 'iam.amazonaws.com/role' is present — this pod lacks that annotation but the chain ordering with Cilium's BPF hooks means the Cilium policy is evaluated first at tc-ingress on the host veth.
